newsitem.title: USA: Barrett drills dry hole offshore Texas.
newsitem.headline: Barrett drills dry hole offshore Texas.

text.p: Barrett Resources Corp said Wednesday its High Island A-545 1 well was a dry hole, while the Mustang Island Block 803 1 well found natural gas.

Both of these wells, located in the Gulf of Mexico offshore Texas, are operated by Barrett with a 100 percent working interest. They were acquired in the September 1996 Federal Offshore Lease Sale 161.
President Paul M. Rady said "We are very disappointed with the dry hole result at the High Island A-545."
He noted the company paid about $13 million for the lease and said the dry hole costs were about $4.2 million.

Barrett said the High Island well was drilled to a depth of 10,513 feet and encountered 350 net feet of wet sand of the Pleistocene Basal Nebraskan formation. Although the sands encountered were thick, porous and high structurally to the downdip control well, their seismic bright spots were apparently the result of low gas saturation. The rig will move off the block and move to Barrett's High Island Block A-364, located about 16 miles southeast off eastern Texas.
Barrett said Mustang Island 803 1 was drilled to 8,900 feet and encountered 75 net feet of natural gas pay in seven sandstone zones of the Miocene Cris "A" Formation.

The company said it has set production casing to total depth, and the well has been temporarily abandoned in preparation to produce. A platform will be installed and production is expected to begin in the third quarter of 1997.
The rig has been moved off of the location and is heading to Barrett's Matagorda Island Block 652/670 prospect, located approximately 35 miles north of the find off south Texas.

Rady said the company plans to drill at least eight more prospects and participate in 16 additional prospects this year as part of its 1997 Program, with a mix of lower risk-type drilling along with higher risk, higher potential prospects.

"Our discovery at Mustang Island 803 will add to our growing production base, and is representative of our larger proportion of lower risk type prospects. These type of wells allow us to drill the smaller proportion of higher risk, high potential prospects."

Last year, the company said, it participated in 17 wells in the Gulf of Mexico. Fourteen of these wells were completed as producers and six are now on-line producing 21 million cubic feet of natural gas per day net to Barrett's working interest. The remaining eight productive wells are scheduled to be on-line over the next three quarters.
